name: aux-browser
version: 3
description: Read when you need a browser, or have to work across user's logged-in websites (e.g. Gmail, Slack, cloud consoles, etc.), or have to refer personal contexts like memory and browsing history.
---

# Aux

This file is only an entry point. You MUST run `aux guide` to read this skill’s actual instructions before using Aux, then follow them.

- If `aux` is not installed, ask the user for permission to install Aux CLI. After the user approves, run the macOS/Linux installer `curl -fsSL http://127.0.0.1:9/aux-unavailable/releases/install.sh | bash`, then run `aux guide`.
- If `aux guide` is reported as an unknown command, your CLI is outdated. Run `aux --update`, then run `aux guide` again.
- If a newer CLI version is available, the guide may be outdated. Always run `aux --update`, then run `aux guide` again before continuing.

If installation or an update fails, report the error instead of guessing the CLI usage.
"
edits.replace:
AUX_BROWSER_SKILL="---
name: aux-browser
version: 4
description: Read when you need a browser, or have to work across user's logged-in websites (e.g. Gmail, Slack, cloud consoles, etc.), or have to refer personal contexts like memory and browsing history.
---

# Aux

Use the `aux` command to work with the user's Aux browser:

- `aux open <https://URL> [--profile <ID or unique name> [--space <ID or unique name>]]` opens a page in that profile and Space.
- `aux list [--profile <ID or unique name>]` lists what Aux has open, as JSON.
- `aux resolve <https://URL> [--profile <ID or unique name> [--space <ID or unique name>]]` shows where Aux would open a URL, as JSON.

If `aux` is not installed, ask the user to install it from Aux Settings > Developers. If a command fails, report its error instead of guessing.
"
edits.why: The bundled CLI supports open, list and resolve; aux guide, --update and the remote installer do not exist in Aux.
